targets.recommended_evidence_quality_note: V3-EXQ-857 (Q-086, environment-confound control for the V3-EXQ-664/856 z_harm_a saturation signature -- the driver's own designated follow-up to V3-EXQ-856's FAIL): precondition_unmet correctly flagged -- the num_hazards(4->1)/hazard_food_attraction(0.7->0.2) manipulation, though large on paper, did not move the sensory harm tier z_harm_s beyond seed noise (cross-arm SNR 0.42 vs the required 2.0 floor). This is likely a STATISTICAL POWER problem rather than a design-logic flaw: per-seed z_harm_s shows large between-seed variance (harsh [0.308, 0.647, 0.421], gentle [0.212, 0.649, 0.299]) relative to the modest cross-arm mean difference (0.072), and only 3 seeds were run. A secondary observation supports the manipulation doing SOMETHING even though the readiness gate didn't clear: min_eval_steps differs sharply between arms (harsh=58 vs gentle=125), suggesting harsher-arm episodes end earlier (plausibly hazard-driven mortality/truncation) -- a signal the per-step z_harm_s average may be diluting rather than capturing. Recommend a redesigned re-run with EITHER (a) more seeds (5-10) to gain power against the observed noise level, or (b) a starker environmental gradient (e.g. num_hazards 4 vs 0, or a larger hazard_food_attraction gap) to widen the expected cross-arm effect relative to the noise floor, or both. Until this readiness gate clears, the representational-pathology vs faithful-ecological-suffering discrimination Q-086 exists to make remains untested, and the 856/857 chain's shared question (what explains the 664 saturation-and-inversion signature) stays open on BOTH candidate explanations (PE-target flag: weakened by 856; environment: untested by 857).
learning_extracted: A large-on-paper parameter change (75% reduction in num_hazards, 71% reduction in hazard_food_attraction) can still fail to clear an SNR-based readiness gate if the underlying metric has high seed-to-seed variance -- 3 seeds is not automatically enough power just because the manipulated parameters look substantial.

The sharply different min_eval_steps between arms (58 vs 125) is a secondary, uncounted signal that the manipulation may be doing something real (episodes ending earlier under the harsh config) that the specific per-step z_harm_s average readout is not capturing -- worth instrumenting directly in a redesign (e.g. episode survival time as an explicit secondary DV).

The 856/857 diagnostic chain (PE-target hypothesis vs environment hypothesis for the 664 signature) has now run both legs without resolving the underlying question -- 856 weakened its hypothesis cleanly, 857 couldn't test its hypothesis at all. The 664 signature's explanation remains genuinely open.
